module_title: Delhi Sultanate - Administration, Policies, and MBT's Experiments
introduction: At this level, we study Alauddin Khalji's market control system and military reforms, alongside Muhammad Bin Tughlaq's (MBT) ambitious but failed administrative experiments, which triggered the decline of the Tughlaq empire.

core_concepts.title: Alauddin Khalji's Military Reforms
core_concepts.description: He started paying soldiers in cash. To prevent corruption in the army, he introduced the system of 'Dagh' (branding of horses) and 'Chehra/Huliya' (maintaining a descriptive roll of soldiers).

core_concepts.title: Market Control Policy
core_concepts.description: To maintain a massive standing army on low salaries, Alauddin strictly fixed the prices of all essential commodities. He appointed officers like 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' and 'Shahna-i-Mandi' to regulate markets.

core_concepts.title: 5 Experiments of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq (MBT)
core_concepts.description: Taxation in Doab, Transfer of Capital (Delhi to Daulatabad), Introduction of Token Currency (copper/brass coins), and the Khurasan and Karachil expeditions. Though visionary, poor execution led to their disastrous failure.

core_concepts.title: Sultanate Architecture
core_concepts.description: This period saw the evolution of 'Indo-Islamic' architecture. Prominent examples include the Alai Darwaza (Alauddin), Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, and the fort of Tughlaqabad.

core_concepts.title: Rise of Vijayanagara and Bahmani
core_concepts.description: Due to MBT's weak grip over the South, rebellions broke out leading to the establishment of the Vijayanagara Empire (1336, by Harihara and Bukka) and the Bahmani Kingdom (1347, by Hasan Gangu).

important_entities.name: Alauddin Khalji
important_entities.significance: Saved Delhi from continuous Mongol invasions and plundered South India (Warangal, Devagiri, Hoysalas) under the leadership of his general Malik Kafur.

important_entities.name: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
important_entities.significance: The most educated Sultan of the era (scholar of Arabic, Persian, astronomy, etc.), but notorious for his highly impractical administrative policies.

important_entities.name: Ibn Battuta
important_entities.significance: Arrived in India during MBT's reign (1333 AD). He wrote the book 'Rihla' and was appointed as the 'Qazi' (judge) of Delhi by the Sultan.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: It wasn't built by a single ruler. Aibak laid the foundation, Iltutmish completed it (added 3 storeys), and later Firoz Shah Tughlaq repaired the top storeys after lightning damage.
MBT did not intend to abandon Delhi permanently. He shifted to Devagiri (renamed Daulatabad) to establish a second capital for better control over the Deccan.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Diwan-i-Arz (Military Dept) was created by Balban. Diwan-i-Kohi (Agriculture Dept) was created by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.

exam_strategy_tips: Questions asking to 'Match the Following' for new departments (Diwans) and their founding Sultans are extremely common.
Memorize the name of Ibn Battuta's book ('Rihla') and the Sultan he visited.
